title: Token Credit Gardener: proportional latency credits with kernel affinity and attention-sparsity signals
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode phase splitting heuristics are brittle when combined with kernel-level preferences and per-tenant latency targets. Some kernels (large-batched, fused-attn) only reach efficiency at larger microbatch sizes. Aggressive phase merging to optimize throughput causes tail-latency regressions for small-REQ latency-sensitive tenants; conversely, strict latency-first splits waste kernel efficiency and raise unit cost.

Goal: Implement a scheduler augmentation ("Token Credit Gardener") that issues proportional latency credits to in-flight requests and reconciles those credits with kernel-affinity hints and attention-sparsity signals to decide dynamic phase merging/splitting. The system should smoothly trade throughput for latency on a per-tenant and per-request basis, improve overall token/sec without increasing p99 for latency-sensitive tenants, and provide observable knobs for ops and product.

Key ideas: 
- Latency credits: assign each request a decaying credit budget derived from tenant SLO and request deadline. Credits prioritize earlier phases (prefill) that are latency-sensitive.
- Kernel affinity hints: runtime exposes per-model kernels with preferred microbatch ranges and efficiency curves. Scheduler consults these hints to avoid merging phases that would push a request into an inefficient kernel regime.
- Attention-sparsity predictor: lightweight estimator (based on prompt features and cached KV signatures) predicts sparse attention opportunities; when high sparsity is expected, merging is more attractive because kernels can exploit sparsity for speed.
- Proportional gardener policy: compute a merge_score = f(credits, kernel_efficiency_delta, sparsity_score, tenant_weight). Positive score => merge phases; negative => split. The gardener also enforces short-term fairness tokens (prevent monopolization) and a starvation guard.

Implementation plan: 
1) Runtime contract: add kernel metadata endpoint with preferred_batch_range and marginal_efficiency curve (shallow JSON) and a lightweight sparsity estimator hook.
2) Scheduler: new module token_credit_gardener with tunable weights; initial heuristic implementation + feature flags.
3) Telemetry: emit decision_reason, estimated_efficiency_delta, resulting_kernel_hint, and credit_balance. Add per-tenant aggregated fairness and latency deltas to console.
4) Experiments: canary rollout on dedicated cluster with A/B: baseline vs gardener-on. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and tenant-level fairness metric (max p99/p50 ratio across tenants).

Risks & mitigations: 
- Inaccurate sparsity predictions could bias merges incorrectly. Mitigate by conservative default weight and open fallback to per-request hedged split.
- Kernel metadata drift across model versions. Mitigate with CI validation and kernel probes during model onboarding.
- Complexity in observability. Mitigate by instrumenting decision_reason and providing aggregated dashboards before rollout.

Rollout: feature-flagged, start on non-critical tenants, 2-week canary, staged expansion with rollback thresholds (p99 uplift > 5% or cost regress > 8% for any tenant).
acceptance_criteria: Gardener module deployed behind feature flag and togglable per-cluster
Telemetry: decision_reason and credit_balance emitted for >=99% of scheduling decisions
Canary A/B run shows <=3% p99 regression for latency-sensitive tenants and >=7% tokens/sec improvement for throughput-heavy test workload
Kernel affinity metadata consumed by scheduler and used in >=95% of merge decisions during canary
Conservative default weights exist so enabling on mixed traffic does not increase average cost per token by >5%
comments: 2025-02-15 - Triage: flagged as P1 since impacts both cost and customer SLOs. Asha + Liam to prototype heuristic in 2 sprints.
2025-02-20 - Design review: PM (Nora Chen) requested per-tenant override and console visibility for credit budgets. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-28 - Eng update: prototype implemented (branch: feat/token-credit-gardener). Kernel metadata API wired to runtime probe. Initial unit tests added.
2025-03-03 - Benchmark: internal microbench shows 9% tokens/sec improvement on condenser-like models with sparsity=0.6 when gardener merges; p95 increased by 1.8ms. Full A/B scheduled.

2025-03-05 - Review feedback from runtime team: prefer numeric marginal_efficiency instead of curve for first iteration; adjusted plan and estimate. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824
